Title: Making ASIC power estimates before the design - EDN
# Making ASIC power estimates before the design. In general, the team responsible for process, IP, and design selection should also own the predesign power estimates. For example, a software-centric architect plus a continually distracted manager will probably generate inadequate predesign ASIC power estimates, causing suboptimal process, design, and IP selection. A check of library and IP availability will quickly help eliminate process choices and reduce the scope of the power-estimation effort before you start your design. Engineers prefer to use spreadsheets for early-phase power estimation because they are easy to use, help organize data, and support what-if design scenarios. Before design start, the process, libraries, IP, and so forth remain undefined, which makes it difficult to estimate power with EDA tools. Using spreadsheets to estimate power consumption represents a rare design-community preference for software from Microsoft, for example, rather than from the EDA industry. ## Memory power estimation. Thus, you can also assume that dynamic memory power—related to switching capacitance—is constant over process and temperature for rough power-estimation purposes. Because switching capacitance is fairly constant over process and temperature, for estimation purposes dynamic power becomes a function of just the voltage squared and the transition frequency. For example, if the memory vendor has provided best-case dynamic power at 1.32V, reflecting a 10% supply variation, but the design operates at or below 1.26V, reflecting a 5% supply variation, the dynamic-power-consumption scaling factor would be (1.26)²/(1.32)²=0.91. For example, assume that memory-vendor specs provide dynamic-power consumption at fixed activity rates, such as 20%, and the design runs at a maximum activity rate of 10%. An alternative approach to making dynamic power estimates involves scaling clock-tree power from a previous similar design. Next, scale for frequency and the load count and then estimate the power per clock in the new design. If targeting the same process node and library, then scale the instance count to make the leakage-power estimate. Finally, scale the standard-cell samples to represent corresponding estimated design-instance counts and calculate the total static-power estimate. Recombine memory, IP, and standard-cell power estimates when necessary. IC design projects differ greatly, so you will need flexibility and engineering judgment to handle design-specific power-estimation issues.

In this article, we will explore the critical role of standard cell libraries in VLSI design, their characteristics, applications, and best practices for utilization. Standard cell libraries are the foundation upon which VLSI designs are constructed. To ensure accurate simulation and analysis of VLSI designs, standard cell libraries must be thoroughly characterized and modeled. A high-quality standard cell library should have the following characteristics: * Accurate characterization and modeling * Robust design and layout * Low power consumption * High speed and performance * Compatibility with a wide range of design tools and flows A reliable standard cell library is essential for ensuring that VLSI designs meet their performance, power, and area (PPA) targets. * Digital signal processing (DSP) design: Standard cell libraries are used to create high-performance DSP circuits for applications such as image and video processing. ### Benefits of Using Standard Cell Libraries in ASIC and FPGA Design The use of standard cell libraries in ASIC and FPGA design offers a number of benefits, including: * Improved design productivity: Standard cell libraries provide a pre-designed and pre-characterized set of cells that can be used to create complex digital circuits quickly and efficiently. * Improved PPA: Standard cell libraries are optimized for performance, power, and area, making it easier to achieve PPA targets in VLSI designs. To get the most out of standard cell libraries, designers should follow best practices for utilization, including selecting the right standard cell library for their design, optimizing standard cell library performance and power consumption, and ensuring standard cell library compatibility and interoperability. results.content:
Title: ASIC-System on Chip-VLSI Design: Libraries In Physical Design
# ASIC-System on Chip-VLSI Design. ### Libraries In Physical Design. Technology libraries are integral part of the ASIC backend EDA tools. Important two libraries are briefly explained below. Technology file defines basic characteristic of cell library pertaining to a particular technology node. They are units used in the design, graphical characteristics like colors, stipple patterns, line styles, physical parameters of metal layers, coupling capacitances, capacitance models, dielectric values, device characteristics, design rules. These specifications are divided into technology file sections. Units for power, voltage, current etc are defined in technology section. The color section defines primary and display colors that a tool uses to display designs in the library. Stipple pattern are defined in stipple sections. Different layer definitions like its current density, width etc are defined in layer section. Fringe capacitances generated by crossing of interconnects are defined in fringe cap section. Similarly several other specifications like metal density, design rules that apply to design in library, place and route (P&R) rules, slot rule, resistance model are defined in their respective sections. **Standard Cell Libraries, I/O Cell Libraries, Special Cell Libraries**. A standard cell library is a collection of pre designed layout of basic logic gates like inverters, buffers, ANDs, ORs, NANDs etc. All the cells in the library have same standard height and have varied width. These standard cell libraries are known as ***reference libraries in Astro***. These reference libraries are technology specific and are generally provided by ASIC vendor like TSMC, Artisan, IBM etc. Standard cell height for 130 TSMC process is 3.65 µM. In addition to standard cell libraries, reference libraries contain I/O and Power/Ground pad cell libraries. It also contain IP libraries for reusable IP like RAMs, ROMs and other pre-designed, standard, complex blocks. The TSMC universal I/O libraries include several power/ground cells that supply different voltages to the core, pre-drivers and post drivers. Internal pull-up or pull-down is provided to some cells in I/O libraries.
